title: The fire on the mountain
hook: on the way home Musa sees a fire and goes to fetch a coal, and is spoken to in the sacred valley of Tuwa
carry: you are in a sacred valley
tomorrow: The staff and the shining hand

segments.voice: Yesterday: water at Madyan, and a stranger who helped first and asked after. Your line was in need of any good. Did any good come walking? Day forty-eight.

Some of the biggest moments of a life begin with an errand. You went out for milk and met the person you married. You took a wrong turn and found the house you'd live in for twenty years. Years have passed at Madyan. Musa has served his time, and now he's traveling with his family, in the dark and the cold. Then, off on the side of a mountain, he sees a fire. He tells his family: wait here. I've spotted a fire. Maybe I can bring you back a burning coal, or find someone there who can show us the way. He's going for a coal. That's all. Today: the fire on the mountain.
screen: `BIG MOMENTS START AS ERRANDS.` → `A FIRE ON THE MOUNTAINSIDE.` → `WAIT HERE.`

segments.voice: Surah Ta-Ha tells what happens when he gets there. He's called by name. O Musa. I am your Lord. So take off your sandals; you are in the sacred valley of Tuwa. And I have chosen you, so listen to what is revealed. Take off your sandals. Before anything else, before the mission, before the signs, the first instruction is about his feet. Commentators have offered more than one reason: out of respect, the way you'd take off your shoes entering a home; or so that he'd feel the holy ground directly, nothing between him and it. The Qur'an doesn't explain. It just asks. Then the heart of what he's told. I am Allah; there is no god but Me. So worship Me, and establish the prayer for My remembrance. Notice what comes first, before Pharaoh, before any rescue: who God is, and prayer. This is why Musa has a special title in Islam: Kalimullah, the one Allah spoke to. The Qur'an says in Surah an-Nisa that Allah spoke to Musa directly. Surah al-Qasas adds that the voice came from a tree, on the right side of the valley. Jews and Christians tell this moment too, as the burning bush in Exodus. And one more thing: Musa didn't climb that mountain looking for God. He was looking for a coal to keep his family warm, and directions home. The sacred valley was right there on his errand. He just had to stop, and take off his shoes.
screen: `O MUSA, I AM YOUR LORD.` · `TAKE OFF YOUR SANDALS.` · `WORSHIP ME, AND PRAY.` · `KALIMULLAH — THE ONE SPOKEN TO.` · then, large: `THE SACRED VALLEY OF TUWA.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: take your shoes off, and stand still. If you can, do it now. Socks are fine too. Stand on whatever floor you're on, carpet, tile, kitchen linoleum, grass. Feel it under your feet. Let your weight settle. Don't try to make the room holy. Just treat it, for two minutes, as if it might be. Breathe slowly. If you pray, you can remember the words: there is no god but Allah. If not, simply stand, and let the ground be the ground. The bell holds the time.
The fire on the mountain. A man who went for a coal, and was told to take off his sandals on sacred ground. Today's word.
screen: `THE FIRE ON THE MOUNTAIN — today's word`.

segments.voice: Your line: you are in a sacred valley. Somewhere in today's errands, stop once, feel your feet, and treat that spot as holy ground. Day forty-eight.

screen: `DAY 48 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: THE STAFF AND THE SHINING HAND.`

howItsDone: Muslims take off their shoes before entering a mosque or stepping onto a prayer space, and Musa is honored with the title Kalimullah, the one to whom Allah spoke.

he went for a burning coal to warm his family, and maybe directions.
the first thing he's told to do is take off his sandals
you are in the sacred valley of Tuwa.
the Qur'an explains why he had to remove his sandals

fork.setup: you're Musa, traveling at night with your family. you see a fire on the mountainside. what do you do?
options: keep moving. fires in the desert mean trouble.
tell your family to wait, and go fetch a coal.
send one of the family to see who's there.
fork.reveal: he goes himself, hoping for a coal or directions, and is called by name: O Musa, I am your Lord. take off your sandals.

original.note: Arabic: "the one Allah spoke to," Musa's title in Islam, drawn from Qur'an 4:164.

trapdoor: what you thought: the burning bush.
what it means: a man on an errand is called by name, told to take off his sandals on sacred ground, and taught first who God is and to pray.
what a scholar hears: Ta-Ha 20:12 names the valley Tuwa; 28:30 places the voice at a tree on the valley's right side; 4:164 is the root of the title Kalimullah.

sources.ref: Exodus 3:1–6 (the burning bush, named as a neighbor)

notes: Reasons for removing the sandals: the script gives two commentary views without choosing (respect; feeling the blessed ground). Some commentaries give others (e.g., the sandals' material). Confirm.
Kalimullah: a traditional title, not a Qur'anic phrase; the note says it draws on 4:164. Confirm spelling and pronunciation.
'Years have passed at Madyan': the Qur'an says he completed the term (28:29) without specifying which.
